title: The Call That Arrived Tomorrow
disclosure: Original declared fiction. Fresh stock footage is retained with source, license, hash and Drive evidence; final publication remains subject to human approval.

story.person: Daniel, an overnight hospital switchboard operator
story.central_question: Why is a disconnected ward calling from tomorrow, and what will Daniel sacrifice to answer it?
story.risk: If Daniel routes the warning, the sealed records room may claim him as its witness; if he destroys it, someone tomorrow may die.
story.irreversible_decision: Daniel connects the line and routes the impossible warning instead of destroying the log.
story.consequence: The hospital goes dark and the final record addresses Daniel with the word home.
story.wound: Daniel has spent eleven years hiding his sister's death inside an official accident report.
story.flaw: He treats burial of evidence as protection from responsibility.
story.something_to_lose: His safety, his self-forgiveness and the possibility of remaining outside the story.
story.hook: At 2:17 a.m., an extension from a dead hospital ward rings for Daniel.
story.reveal: The warning was not only about tomorrow; answering it makes Daniel the next address in the record.

beats.text: Daniel was alone at the hospital switchboard when a dead extension rang.
The number belonged to the ward disconnected eleven years earlier, the night his sister died.
He answered. No voice spoke, only breathing, then three words: Don't send the elevator.
The call ended. The switchboard printed tomorrow's emergency log, signed with Daniel's name.
On the fourth floor, one elevator button was warm.
Beneath it, a red light glowed behind the sealed records room.
Daniel had filed his sister's death as an accident.
Now the call replayed the minute he refused to remember.
In the original log, he found the rule: every answered call demanded a witness.
Destroy the page, and the past stayed buried. Route it, and someone tomorrow might live.
Daniel connected the line. Hospital went dark. the receiver rang from inside the sealed room.
At dawn, the new log held one completed call: Daniel's name—followed by home.
